thread.title_full: Miller-Meeks highlights tax relief for working families with new legislation on Tax Day

author: Hawkeye Reporter
title: Miller-Meeks highlights tax relief for working families with new legislation on Tax Day
text:
Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks announced on Apr. 15 that the Working Families Tax Cuts are delivering what she described as the largest tax relief for working and middle-class Americans in U.S. history.
The announcement comes at a time when many families have faced increased living costs, and supporters say the new law aims to provide significant financial relief to a wide range of groups, including workers, seniors, farmers, and small businesses. The legislation passed without support from any Democrats in Congress.
“After four years of record-high inflation under the Biden Administration, where everything from housing to healthcare became more expensive, American families needed real relief,” said Congresswoman Miller-Meeks. “That’s exactly what the Working Families Tax Cuts deliver—the largest tax cut in American history, putting thousands of dollars back into the pockets of working families. This law reduces taxes on tips and overtime, provides relief for seniors on Social Security, doubles the Child Tax Credit, and lowers the burden on small businesses, farmers, and manufacturers, while also protecting taxpayer dollars by ensuring benefits go to those here legally. This is about rewarding hard work, restoring opportunity, and helping families get ahead again, and I was proud to deliver it.”
The Working Families Tax Cuts include reduced taxes on tips and overtime pay; new deductions for seniors receiving Social Security; a doubled Child Tax Credit; an increased standard deduction; a permanent 20 percent deduction for small businesses; policies supporting manufacturing and energy production; targeted support for rural communities; $1,000 investment accounts for newborns; and measures that remove illegal immigrants from Medicaid and SNAP eligibility.
Miller-Meeks is currently serving in Congress representing Iowa’s 1st district after replacing Dave Loebsack in 2021 according to public records. She has served since then following her previous term in the Iowa Senate from 2019 to 2021 as reported by legislative sources. Miller-Meeks was born in Herlong, California in 1955 and now lives in Le Claire according to biographical information available online. She graduated from Texas Christian University with a Bachelor of Science degree in Nursing (BSN) in 1976.
As Americans file their taxes this year under these new provisions—many are seeing larger refunds or bigger paychecks than before.
